text:
Amy_S: Hey team, hitting a weird hang in the Python SDK streaming path. Generator yields fine, then after a reconnect+keepalive boundary it blocks and emits a partial token fragment. Repro below.

Roberto_Eng: Can you paste the minimal repro + versions?

Amy_S: Sure — env: Python 3.11, redwood-python 0.9.2, requests 2.31.0. Behavior: streaming generator yields tokens, then we get a keepalive (`data: \"\n\"`) and a reconnect. After reconnect the generator yields nothing (hang). Logs show a partial utf-8 chunk that never completes, e.g. \"\u00c3\" and then nothing.

Jin_ML: That sounds like an SSE frame boundary being split mid-codepoint. Could be our byte-slicing on reconnect. Any stacktrace?

Amy_S: Minimal repro attached as gist (snipped inline):
```py
import redwood
client = redwood.Client(api_key=...)
gen = client.stream("chat.completions", model="open-short", prompt="hi", keepalive=20)
for chunk in gen:
    print(chunk, end='')
# After ~30s we simulate a network reconnect (SIGPIPE in our infra) and the generator never resumes.
```

Maya_SE: Do you see the generator yield a final "data: [partial]" event before the reconnect?

Amy_S: Yes, logs: `event: message\ndata: \"par\`` then reconnect, then next connection resumes with `data: \"tial_token\"` but our generator doesn't stitch them.

Roberto_Eng: That explains it. Our SSE parser assumes each event is fully received before handing to the generator. If a keepalive forces a reconnect and the server split a token across connections, the parser currently drops the incomplete buffer on reconnect.

Jin_ML: Can you run with env var REDWOOD_SSE_DEBUG=1 and paste the raw frames? Also which transport — HTTP/1.1 SSE emulation over chunked, or real SSE?

Amy_S: It's HTTP/1.1 chunked SSE. Debug output (sanitized):
```
[conn1] recv: b"event: message\n"
[conn1] recv: b"data: \"par"
[conn1] keepalive: b"\n"
[conn1] conn reset by peer
[conn2] new conn
[conn2] recv: b"data: tial_token\"\n\n"
```

Maya_SE: OK that's clear. The client should buffer across reconnection boundaries and concatenate partial data segments for the same logical event. Right now it abandons the buffer on connection loss.

Roberto_Eng: Quick mitigation: upgrade to redwood-python 0.9.4 (unreleased patch) that I can drop into your env; it preserves the partial event buffer across reconnects. Want me to push a wheel to your workspace?

Amy_S: Yes please — that would help validate. Also note this only reproducible if keepalive occurs between byte boundaries (rare). We have a customer hit and they see intermittent generator stalls.

eng_oncall_bot: @channel Escalation created: INC-2891 — python streaming generator hang on reconnect. Assigned to eng-ml.

Jin_ML: If you can't take the patched wheel, you can workaround by disabling client-side reconnects and let app-level retry logic re-init the stream (less ideal). Also set keepalive interval longer.

Amy_S: Patch test: installed 0.9.4-pre from Roberto. Ran the same repro 10x, no hangs so far. Partial fragments are now merged and the generator yields full tokens. :thumbsup:

Maya_SE: Great. Can you capture pcap + raw server frames and drop in INC-2891 for postmortem? We'll also add an integration test that simulates split multi-byte utf8 across SSE reconnects.

Roberto_Eng: I'll open a PR with unit + integration tests and mark release as 0.9.4. Will coordinate with release team for a patch release and a short advisory.

Amy_S: Thanks all. For the customer I've applied the patched wheel and they report reduced incidents. I'll keep INC-2891 updated with customer logs and the verification steps.

support-bot: Note: Billing unaffected. No retries triggered by chargeable actions.

Roberto_Eng: Follow-up: adding a telemetry gauge for "sse.partial_bytes_lost" so we can measure frequency of these reconnect-split events.

Amy_S: Appreciated. Leaving this thread open until the patch is published to PyPI and the customer confirms no regression.

Maya_SE: TL;DR: root cause = SSE parser dropping partial event buffer on reconnect causing generator hang on multi-byte split; fix in 0.9.4 preserves buffer and stitches fragments.
